content:
The recent changes to the e-cog, is actually bad.
Reason being: 
1. New player might see it as P2W predatory prompt.
2. It's not an actually needed changes.

Imagine this:
You are a new player, you don't know left and right. No idea what currency is what.
You are defeated in the stages, suddenly a prompt asking if you want to buy e-cog appear.

What do you think will the new player think?
There is definitely some player that will think like this upon seeing the e-cog purchase prompt:
"WTF, the game feels predatory, this must be the p2w solution, let's stay away from this game. No modern gacha does this outdated shit" and POOF, a newbie gone

Overall, it does minimal impact to your existing players.
I know some of it's positive side, but
I personally see it as minor negative change, as it reduce my agency on resource management.
I'm sure that it will affect some new player retention NEGATIVELY.

I am not expecting a grand or complex answer.
I fully understand that this takes time and is not a decision that can be made lightly.
The problem, however, is that people are completely unaware of the current situation.
We used to love this game because communication with the players was quick and frequent, but that is certainly not the case anymore. There is even speculation circulating that the service might be shutting down.
If you need more time, please simply post a notice to let us know.
Without any communication, people will continue to speculate, and the narrative will inevitably take a turn for the worse.

Even if you plan to announce your thoughts, the company's position, or future direction at a later date, responding to the current situation with silence—without taking any action—is the worst possible move.

I feel ashamed that I was the one who introduced this game to my friends.

I have played Morimens for 666 hours because I genuinely loved this game. I recommended it to my friends countless times because I believed this was a world worth supporting and protecting.

That is why this patch and the developers’ response hurt so much.

My friends are already preparing to quit, simply waiting for what feels like a final ultimatum. I cannot blame them. Many of us stayed because we trusted the developers, believed in the game’s direction, and wanted to see Morimens grow.

I told my friends, “Let’s wait. Let’s give the developers a chance. They will listen.”

Now, I feel foolish for having said that.

I am not asking for compensation or special treatment. I am asking for something much simpler: acknowledge your mistakes, explain your decisions, and communicate with us to find a reasonable compromise.

I understand that difficult content can provide a great sense of accomplishment. But not every player enjoys extreme difficulty. Many of us enjoy progressing step by step, challenging ourselves at a reasonable level and earning rewards that match our efforts.

Please don’t hide behind the achievements of top-tier players.

Give us choices. Add different difficulty levels with appropriate rewards, and let players choose the experience that suits them.

We are not asking you to abandon your vision for Morimens. We are asking you to build that vision with us.

A game cannot exist without the players who choose to remain in its world. And if there is no world left for us to protect, we can no longer be its guardians.

We still care about Morimens. That is why we are speaking up.

Please listen to us one more time.

I don’t want to regret the 666 hours I spent in this world.
I don’t want to regret introducing this game to my friends.

Give us a reason to trust you again.

Dear development team of our beloved Lovecraftian gacha game, Morimens,

Right now, the game is clearly experiencing an alarming decline in player interest and willingness to continue playing. Many players are openly declaring that they no longer intend to support the game. It is clear that any gacha game will have power creep, as it is both a fundamental part of the genre and a monetization option. However, what is happening in the game right now genuinely worries me, and it feels as though the development team has absolutely no idea what it is doing.

Even if you urgently needed to increase the level of power creep, that does not mean the game needed such a large scale D-Tide update. What has happened does not benefit either you or the players. Besides its Lovecraftian setting, Morimens' biggest selling point has always been the ability to create different teams based on character mechanics and different playstyles. What has happened has not only ruined the experience for new players and created problems with clearing content, but has also destroyed this defining feature. What is the point of trying to create interesting teams by building a diverse range of characters if only a few team types -mostly consisting of the same characters - are currently suitable for the most difficult content?

Restricting content to specific levels of investment in specific characters is definitely one of the worst things a gacha game can do, and no relatively popular gacha game embraces this approach. Every time another gacha development team tries it, it usually lasts for only one version if it even gets past beta testing.

At the same time, there is no point in players investing in characters who cannot deal HP%-based damage, survive for long periods, or scale very quickly. Team diversity has been ruined, people’s desire to invest in the game has been ruined, and their desire to continue supporting the game has been ruined.

content:
The upcoming HP and damage reduction changes to D-tide are helpful and probably sufficient as a bandaid fix for the current cycle, but I don't think they address the issue of reduced player choice.

- The vast majority of casual players used to hang around A2-A4, giving them three difficulty options. Now they only have two, as clearing madness isn't really a viable option for most of them, and presumably won't be even with the nerfs.

- In the old system players had a choice between vertical and horizontal investment. If their teams couldn't clear a specific difficulty, they could choose to clear the difficulty below twice and have the bonus clear reward make up for the reduced difficulty score. Most players still consider 400 points as the "goal", but in the new system you need two bonus clears to make up for a missed clear on a higher difficulty.

Under the previous system, players could choose anything between 5 Alert 5 clears and 10 Alert 4 clears to reach 400 points. Currently it is impossible to reach 400 points with Normal mode clears and it requires at least 3 Hard clears, with Hard difficulty intended to be similar to Alert 5. 
Additionally, under the previous system the Waves were relatively close in power, so a player could choose which waves they would skip A5 on, based on matchups and relics. For example, they could choose to double clear waves 3 and 4 because they prefer repeating the shorter stages. Currently, the massive difference in power between Wave 1 and Wave 5 and Normal and Hard prevents the player from making that choice. The current "easiest" clear always skips W4 and W5 hard. You also need four extra teams to make up for it instead of two.
The nerfs don't really address this issue, at best they'll make W4 hard more accessible, allowing people to choose between a 9 team and a 7 team clear. In that case bonus clears will almost certainly still be set in stone, W5 Normal and W1 hard, as they're significantly easier than the alternatives.

New dtide proposed changes posit no change at all to Normal. This is not tenable. If my fellows in Normal cannot play, I cannot play. I support newbies. Fix Normal W4 W5. Go back to Alert system. This system is bad.

This was my steam review, dropping it here too since nothing was addressed, not just dtide but oh well:
 I had previously reviewed this game positively, but as it stands now, 3 months after I started, the devs have consistently made baffling decisions that leave the game in an objectively worse state than it was 3 months ago.

 They've completely butchered the most enjoyable endgame mode and made many people not even want to touch it. They previously PROMISED that when they added new power levels to characters that you can unlock after pulling 16 copies, that the endgame modes would not be balanced around this level of investment. They lied, and to that effect, even the whales with EVERY character at max investment are struggling to clear now. 

They've nerfed a character that wasn't particularly strong to begin with under the guise of a "bug fix" in order to avoid having to compensate players for the nerf. This character and the WoD (weapon) that was previously BiS on her were both also rerun right before the nerf, so people have spend lots of money on this combo only to have the interaction between them immediately removed after over a year of the interaction being in the game.

 They've gutted a system which allows you to gain affinity with your characters, which is essential to view character stories in the game, which means those stories are now functionally impossible to unlock on certain characters with less active playstyles. 

They previously released a character last month that I bought 4 extra duplicates of specifically because I liked the voice acting the character had. They then bait-and-switched me by removing those voice lines entirely and providing me no compensation for the extra pulls I had spent. This character, which was only released last month, is now also nearly useless in the endgame mode because of the previously mentioned butchering, due to her playstyle not working well with the way they retuned the mode which only adds salt to the wound.

From the perspective of a long term whale who used to love getting 425 in dtide, the changes do nothing to fix what an awful mode high-level dtide has become. Using cheese teams and predetermined setups, fishing for discovers and DR procs, and abusing turn rewind for hours to clear madness is so incredibly tedious and uninteresting. And many of the +12 limited awakeners I invested into, including recent ones, are useless now other than as stat sticks, because you need hyper specific strategies to scale enough damage for madness hp. 

I started playing this game a year ago because it had interesting team building and difficult but thoughtful gameplay, reminiscent of many of my favorite deckbuilders. But the innovation and creativity in Morimen’s end game modes are gone. I now dread playing the tedious slog that used to be my favorite game mode in gachas. Maybe other whales like the new madness dtide (though I haven’t met any), but whatever the case I’ve come to accept that this game is no longer for me.
Roll back to the old version of dtide. You have failed.
